scenario_summary: A journey through permutations and combinations using abstract mathematical sets and formulas.
visual_setting: Mathematical notation, geometric primitives, and clean text labels

scenes.title: Factorial Basics
scenes.narration: In mathematics, the factorial of a number n, denoted by n!, is the product of all positive integers less than or equal to n. For example, 4! = 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 24.
scenes.animation_description: A formula for factorial appears on the screen: n! = n × (n-1) × (n-2) × ... × 1. An arrow points to the variable n.
scenes.manim_hint: Use MathTex to display the factorial formula.

scenes.title: Evaluate 8! and 4! - 3!
scenes.narration: To evaluate 8!, we multiply all integers from 1 to 8. For 4! - 3!, we first calculate 4! and 3!, then subtract the results.
scenes.animation_description: The formula 8! = 8 × 7 × 6 × 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 fades in. The formula 4! - 3! = 24 - 6 = 18 appears below.
scenes.manim_hint: Use MathTex to display the results of the calculations.

scenes.title: Check if 3! + 4! = 7!
scenes.narration: Let's check if the sum of 3! and 4! equals 7!.
scenes.animation_description: The formula 3! + 4! = 6 + 24 = 30 appears on the screen. An arrow points to the result.
scenes.manim_hint: Use MathTex to display the result of the calculation.

scenes.title: Solve for x
scenes.narration: Given the equation 6! × 2! = 7! ÷ x, let's solve for x.
scenes.animation_description: The equation 6! × 2! = 7! ÷ x fades in. The formula x = 7! ÷ (6! × 2!) appears below.
scenes.manim_hint: Use MathTex to display the solution.

scenes.title: Evaluate n! / (n-r)! for n=6, r=2
scenes.narration: Let's evaluate n! / (n-r)! for n=6 and r=2.
scenes.animation_description: The formula n! / (n-r)! = 6! / (6-2)! = 6! / 4! fades in. The result 6! / 4! = 15 appears below.
scenes.manim_hint: Use MathTex to display the result of the calculation.

scenes.title: Evaluate n! / (n-r)! for n=9, r=5
scenes.narration: Let's evaluate n! / (n-r)! for n=9 and r=5.
scenes.animation_description: The formula n! / (n-r)! = 9! / (9-5)! = 9! / 4! fades in. The result 9! / 4! = 126 appears below.
scenes.manim_hint: Use MathTex to display the result of the calculation.

scenes.title: Recap
scenes.narration: In this video, we learned how to evaluate factorials, solve equations involving factorials, and use the formula n! / (n-r)! to find the number of permutations.
scenes.animation_description: A recap slide appears with key formulas and concepts. Text labels explain each formula.
